payers.label: Medicare
payers.priorAuthNote: Medicare generally does not require prior authorization for medically necessary peripheral artery disease interventions, but documentation must support medical necessity.
payers.overview: Medicare covers endovascular revascularization procedures for PAD when deemed medically necessary and performed in an appropriate setting. Coverage typically follows national and local coverage determinations (NCD/LCDs).
payers.reimbursementNote: Reimbursement is based on the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) and Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) rates. RVUs are assigned to each CPT code.

sections.heading: Coverage Criteria: Clinical Indications
items: Symptomatic PAD (e.g., claudication, rest pain, non-healing wounds)
Objective evidence of PAD (e.g., ABI < 0.9, significant stenosis on imaging)
Failure of conservative management (e.g., exercise, risk factor modification)
Procedure performed by a qualified physician in an appropriate facility

sections.heading: Coverage Criteria: Vessel Specific Criteria
items: Significant stenosis or occlusion (typically >50-70%) in target vessel
Lesion amenable to endovascular treatment

sections.heading: Required Documentation: Patient History and Physical
items: Detailed history of PAD symptoms and duration
Physical examination findings (e.g., diminished pulses, skin changes)
Assessment of functional limitations due to PAD

sections.heading: Required Documentation: Diagnostic Test Results
items: Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) measurements
Duplex ultrasound, CTA, or MRA reports demonstrating vessel pathology
Angiography reports, if performed

sections.heading: Required Documentation: Conservative Management
items: Documentation of supervised exercise program, if applicable
Records of pharmacotherapy (e.g., antiplatelets, statins) and lifestyle modifications

sections.heading: Submission Process
items: Ensure all medical records support medical necessity as per NCD/LCDs.
Submit claims with appropriate CPT and ICD-10 codes.
Respond promptly to any Additional Documentation Requests (ADRs).

sections.heading: Common Denial Reasons
items: Lack of documented medical necessity
Insufficient documentation of conservative therapy failure
Inappropriate coding or modifier usage
Services considered experimental or investigational

sections.heading: Authorization Tips
items: Thoroughly document all symptoms, physical findings, and functional limitations.
Clearly state the failure of conservative management strategies.
Reference relevant NCD/LCDs in your documentation.

knownPolicies.notes: Follows NCD 20.7 for Percutaneous Transluminal Angioplasty (PTA).

payers.label: Medicaid
payers.priorAuthNote: Medicaid programs often require prior authorization for endovascular PAD procedures. Requirements vary by state.
payers.overview: Medicaid coverage for PAD interventions varies by state. Most states require prior authorization and adherence to specific medical necessity criteria, often similar to Medicare but with additional administrative steps.
payers.reimbursementNote: Reimbursement rates are determined by individual state Medicaid programs and may differ from Medicare rates.

sections.heading: Coverage Criteria: Clinical Indications
items: Severe claudication limiting daily activities
Rest pain or tissue loss (ulcers, gangrene)
Objective evidence of significant arterial disease
Documented failure of medical management and lifestyle changes

sections.heading: Required Documentation: Authorization Request Form
items: Completed state-specific prior authorization form
Physician order for the procedure

sections.heading: Required Documentation: Medical Records
items: Recent history and physical examination notes
Relevant diagnostic imaging reports (e.g., angiogram, duplex ultrasound)
Documentation of previous treatments and their outcomes

sections.heading: Submission Process
items: Verify state-specific Medicaid guidelines for PAD interventions.
Submit prior authorization request with all required documentation.
Await approval before scheduling the procedure.
Submit claims with the approved authorization number.

sections.heading: Common Denial Reasons
items: Lack of prior authorization
Incomplete or insufficient documentation
Failure to meet state-specific medical necessity criteria
Procedure considered elective or cosmetic

sections.heading: Authorization Tips
items: Always check the specific Medicaid policy for your state.
Submit prior authorization requests well in advance.
Ensure all supporting documentation is comprehensive and clearly linked to medical necessity.

knownPolicies.notes: Specific criteria for claudication and critical limb ischemia.

payers.label: Private Insurance
payers.priorAuthNote: Most private insurance plans require prior authorization for endovascular PAD procedures. Requirements vary significantly by plan.
payers.overview: Private insurance coverage for PAD interventions is highly variable. Most plans require prior authorization and have specific medical policies that outline coverage criteria, which may include a trial of conservative therapy.
payers.reimbursementNote: Reimbursement rates are based on negotiated contracts between the provider and the private insurance company.

sections.heading: Coverage Criteria: Medical Necessity
items: Significant functional impairment due to PAD symptoms
Objective evidence of hemodynamically significant stenosis
Documented failure of at least 3-6 months of conservative therapy (e.g., exercise, medication)

sections.heading: Coverage Criteria: Exclusions
items: Asymptomatic PAD (unless specific high-risk features)
Procedures for cosmetic purposes

sections.heading: Required Documentation: Clinical Records
items: Physician office notes detailing symptoms, physical exam, and impact on quality of life
Results of non-invasive vascular studies (ABI, PVR, duplex ultrasound)
Angiographic images and reports

sections.heading: Required Documentation: Prior Authorization Form
items: Completed and signed prior authorization request form
Letter of medical necessity from the treating physician

sections.heading: Submission Process
items: Review the patient's specific insurance policy for PAD intervention coverage.
Submit a comprehensive prior authorization request, including all clinical documentation.
Follow up with the insurance company regularly for status updates.
Appeal any denials with additional clinical information if appropriate.

sections.heading: Common Denial Reasons
items: Lack of prior authorization
Failure to meet medical policy criteria (e.g., insufficient trial of conservative therapy)
Inadequate documentation of symptoms or objective findings
Procedure considered experimental or investigational by the plan

sections.heading: Authorization Tips
items: Always verify benefits and prior authorization requirements with the specific plan.
Provide detailed clinical notes emphasizing the severity of symptoms and functional impairment.
Highlight the failure of conservative treatments and the necessity of the intervention.

knownPolicies.notes: Requires 3-month trial of conservative therapy for claudication.
Specific criteria for critical limb ischemia and claudication.

customSections.heading: About these measures
customSections.text: Seven Performance Measures (PM-1 – PM-7), appropriate for public reporting and pay-for-performance, and eight Quality Measures (QM-1 – QM-8), for internal quality improvement, derived from the 2026 ACC/AHA Clinical Performance and Quality Measures for PAD and the 2024 ACC/AHA PAD Guideline. General exclusion rule: for all measures except PM-6 and PM-7, a clinician-documented determination that care is inappropriate excludes the patient; for all measures, patients who decline care are excluded. Supervised exercise therapy (PM-7) is Medicare-covered for symptomatic PAD.

customSections.heading: PM-1 — Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) Testing (Performance Measure)
customSections.text:
Patients with suspected or established PAD who have ABI testing documented within 12 months of the encounter.

**Numerator:** Patients with documented ABI measurement within 12 months of the qualifying encounter.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with a diagnosis of PAD or clinical suspicion of PAD (e.g., exertional leg symptoms, non-healing wound, absent pulses).
**Exclusions:** Patients for whom ABI testing is clinically inappropriate (e.g., non-compressible vessels, known severe calcification) — clinician-documented exclusion; Patients who decline ABI testing
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE B-NR
**Rationale:** The ABI is the gold-standard non-invasive test for diagnosing PAD. An ABI ≤0.90 is diagnostic of PAD. Consistent documentation ensures appropriate diagnosis and risk stratification.

customSections.heading: PM-2 — Statin Therapy for PAD (Performance Measure)
customSections.text:
Patients with established PAD who are prescribed statin therapy for lipid management and cardiovascular risk reduction.

**Numerator:** Patients with PAD who are prescribed statin therapy or have documented statin therapy at the qualifying encounter.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with established PAD (ABI ≤0.90 or prior lower extremity revascularization or amputation for PAD).
**Exclusions:** Patients with documented statin intolerance or contraindication (e.g., active liver disease, prior rhabdomyolysis); Patients who decline statin therapy
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE A
**Rationale:** High-intensity statin therapy reduces major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and major adverse limb events (MALE) in patients with PAD. Statin use is a Class 1, LOE A recommendation in the 2024 ACC/AHA PAD Guideline.

customSections.heading: PM-3 — Antithrombotic Therapy for PAD (Performance Measure)
customSections.text:
Patients with symptomatic PAD (claudication, CLTI, or prior revascularization) who are prescribed antithrombotic therapy (antiplatelet or anticoagulant).

**Numerator:** Patients with symptomatic PAD who are prescribed antiplatelet therapy (aspirin, clopidogrel, or low-dose rivaroxaban + aspirin) or therapeutic anticoagulation.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with symptomatic PAD (claudication, CLTI, or prior lower extremity revascularization).
**Exclusions:** Patients with documented contraindication to antithrombotic therapy (e.g., active major bleeding, severe thrombocytopenia); Patients who decline antithrombotic therapy
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE A  ·  New in 2026
**Rationale:** Antithrombotic therapy (single antiplatelet or low-dose rivaroxaban + aspirin) reduces MACE and MALE in symptomatic PAD. This is a Class 1 recommendation in the 2024 ACC/AHA PAD Guideline.

customSections.heading: PM-4 — Blood Pressure Management (Performance Measure)
customSections.text:
Patients with PAD and hypertension who have blood pressure measured and documented with a management plan targeting SBP <130 mmHg.

**Numerator:** Patients with PAD and hypertension who have documented blood pressure measurement AND a documented management plan (pharmacotherapy or lifestyle modification) at the qualifying encounter.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with established PAD and a diagnosis of hypertension.
**Exclusions:** Patients for whom blood pressure management is clinically inappropriate (clinician-documented); Patients who decline blood pressure management
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE A  ·  New in 2026
**Rationale:** Hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for PAD progression and cardiovascular events. Target SBP <130 mmHg is consistent with the 2024 ACC/AHA PAD Guideline and 2017 ACC/AHA Hypertension Guideline.

customSections.heading: PM-5 — ACE Inhibitor / ARB Therapy (Performance Measure)
customSections.text:
Patients with symptomatic PAD who are prescribed ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy for cardiovascular risk reduction.

**Numerator:** Patients with symptomatic PAD who are prescribed an ACE inhibitor or ARB at the qualifying encounter.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with symptomatic PAD (claudication, CLTI, or prior revascularization).
**Exclusions:** Patients with documented contraindication to ACE inhibitors and ARBs (e.g., bilateral renal artery stenosis, prior angioedema, pregnancy, hyperkalemia); Patients who decline ACE inhibitor/ARB therapy
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE A  ·  New in 2026
**Rationale:** ACE inhibitors and ARBs reduce cardiovascular mortality and MACE in patients with PAD. Ramipril demonstrated a 22% relative risk reduction in cardiovascular events in the HOPE trial. This is a Class 1, LOE A recommendation.

customSections.heading: PM-6 — Tobacco Use Screening and Cessation Counseling (Performance Measure)
customSections.text:
Patients with PAD who are screened for tobacco use, and if current users, are offered cessation counseling and pharmacotherapy.

**Numerator:** Patients with PAD who are screened for tobacco use AND, if current users, are offered cessation counseling and pharmacotherapy (varenicline, bupropion, or NRT).
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with established PAD.
**Exclusions:** Patients who decline tobacco screening; Patients who decline cessation counseling or pharmacotherapy (if current users)
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 3 (Harm) / LOE A
**Rationale:** Tobacco use is the most powerful modifiable risk factor for PAD incidence, progression, and limb loss. Continued smoking after revascularization dramatically worsens outcomes. Cessation counseling + pharmacotherapy is Class 3 (Harm) for continued smoking — meaning continued tobacco use is harmful. PM-6 does NOT have the general clinician-appropriateness exclusion.

customSections.heading: PM-7 — Supervised Exercise Therapy (SET) Referral (Performance Measure)
customSections.text:
Patients with claudication symptoms who are referred to or enrolled in a supervised exercise therapy (SET) program.

**Numerator:** Patients with claudication who have a documented referral to or enrollment in a supervised exercise therapy program.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with PAD and claudication symptoms.
**Exclusions:** Patients who decline supervised exercise therapy referral; Patients with CLTI (rest pain, tissue loss) — SET is not indicated for CLTI
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE A
**Rationale:** Supervised exercise therapy is the most effective non-invasive treatment for claudication, improving walking distance, quality of life, and cardiovascular outcomes. It is a Class 1, LOE A recommendation and is Medicare-covered for symptomatic PAD. PM-7 does NOT have the general clinician-appropriateness exclusion.

customSections.heading: QM-1 — Diabetes Management in PAD (Quality Measure)
customSections.text:
Patients with PAD and diabetes mellitus who have HbA1c measured and a documented diabetes management plan.

**Numerator:** Patients with PAD and diabetes who have documented HbA1c measurement AND a diabetes management plan (pharmacotherapy or referral to endocrinology/diabetes educator) at the qualifying encounter.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with established PAD and a diagnosis of diabetes mellitus.
**Exclusions:** Patients for whom diabetes management is clinically inappropriate (clinician-documented); Patients who decline diabetes management
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE B-NR  ·  New in 2026
**Rationale:** Diabetes is a major risk factor for PAD severity, wound healing failure, and amputation. HbA1c target <7% (or individualized) reduces microvascular and macrovascular complications. This is a new 2026 measure reflecting the growing importance of cardiometabolic risk management in PAD.

customSections.heading: QM-2 — Preventive Foot Care (Quality Measure)
customSections.text:
Patients with PAD and diabetes or CLTI who receive preventive foot care education and examination.

**Numerator:** Patients with PAD and diabetes or CLTI who have documented foot examination AND foot care education (self-inspection, footwear, wound prevention) at the qualifying encounter.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with established PAD and either diabetes mellitus or CLTI (rest pain, ischemic ulcer, or gangrene).
**Exclusions:** Patients for whom foot care is clinically inappropriate (clinician-documented); Patients who decline foot care education or examination
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE B-NR  ·  New in 2026
**Rationale:** Foot complications (ulceration, infection, gangrene) are the leading cause of amputation in patients with PAD and diabetes. Preventive foot care reduces amputation rates. This is a new 2026 quality measure.

customSections.heading: QM-3 — Novel Lipid-Lowering Therapy Consideration (Quality Measure)
customSections.text:
Patients with PAD and LDL-C above goal despite maximally tolerated statin therapy who are considered for novel lipid-lowering agents (PCSK9 inhibitors, inclisiran, bempedoic acid, ezetimibe).

**Numerator:** Patients with PAD, LDL-C ≥70 mg/dL despite maximally tolerated statin therapy, who have documented consideration of or prescription for novel lipid-lowering agents.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with established PAD and LDL-C ≥70 mg/dL despite maximally tolerated statin therapy.
**Exclusions:** Patients for whom novel lipid-lowering therapy is clinically inappropriate (clinician-documented); Patients who decline novel lipid-lowering therapy
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 2a (Moderate) / LOE B-R  ·  New in 2026
**Rationale:** PCSK9 inhibitors (evolocumab, alirocumab) reduce MACE in high-risk PAD patients. Bempedoic acid and inclisiran are additional options for statin-intolerant patients. LDL-C <70 mg/dL is the target for very high-risk PAD. This is a new 2026 quality measure reflecting emerging evidence.

customSections.heading: QM-4 — Health Disparities Assessment (Quality Measure)
customSections.text:
Patients with PAD who have race/ethnicity, social determinants of health (SDOH), and access-to-care barriers documented to evaluate disparities in PAD detection and management.

**Numerator:** Patients with PAD who have documented race/ethnicity AND at least one SDOH domain (e.g., food insecurity, housing instability, transportation barriers, insurance status) at the qualifying encounter.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with established PAD.
**Exclusions:** Patients who decline to provide race/ethnicity or SDOH information
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE C-LD  ·  New in 2026
**Rationale:** Black, Hispanic, and low-income patients have significantly higher rates of PAD, amputation, and mortality. Systematic documentation of disparities enables targeted quality improvement. This is a new 2026 quality measure reflecting the ACC/AHA's commitment to health equity.

customSections.heading: QM-5 — Saphenous Vein Assessment Prior to Revascularization (Quality Measure)
customSections.text:
Patients undergoing lower extremity surgical revascularization who have preoperative saphenous vein mapping documented.

**Numerator:** Patients undergoing lower extremity bypass surgery who have documented preoperative duplex ultrasound saphenous vein mapping.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with PAD undergoing lower extremity bypass surgery (femoral-popliteal or femoral-tibial bypass).
**Exclusions:** Patients undergoing endovascular-only revascularization (no bypass surgery planned); Emergency revascularization for acute limb ischemia where preoperative mapping is not feasible; Patients for whom vein mapping is clinically inappropriate (clinician-documented); Patients who decline vein mapping
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE B-NR  ·  New in 2026
**Rationale:** Autologous saphenous vein is the preferred conduit for infrainguinal bypass. Preoperative vein mapping identifies suitable conduit, reduces operative time, and improves patency rates. This is a new 2026 quality measure.

customSections.heading: QM-6 — Multidisciplinary Team Discussion for CLTI (Quality Measure)
customSections.text:
Patients with CLTI who have a documented multidisciplinary team discussion of treatment options (revascularization vs. primary amputation vs. medical management) prior to definitive treatment.

**Numerator:** Patients with CLTI who have documented multidisciplinary team discussion (involving at minimum vascular surgery or IR and wound care or podiatry) prior to definitive treatment.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with CLTI (rest pain, ischemic ulcer, or gangrene) being considered for revascularization or amputation.
**Exclusions:** Patients with acute limb ischemia requiring emergency revascularization; Patients for whom multidisciplinary discussion is not feasible (e.g., rural setting without specialist access) — clinician-documented; Patients who decline multidisciplinary evaluation
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE B-NR  ·  New in 2026
**Rationale:** CLTI is associated with 30% 1-year mortality and 25% major amputation rate. Multidisciplinary team discussions improve limb salvage rates and reduce unnecessary amputations. The BEST-CLI trial demonstrated that surgical bypass with adequate conduit is superior to endovascular therapy in good surgical candidates. This is a new 2026 quality measure.

customSections.heading: QM-7 — Shared Decision-Making Documentation (Quality Measure)
customSections.text:
Patients with PAD who have documented shared decision-making discussion of treatment risks, benefits, and patient preferences.

**Numerator:** Patients with PAD who have documented shared decision-making discussion (including patient preferences, treatment options, risks/benefits) at the qualifying encounter.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with established PAD being considered for revascularization or major medical therapy change.
**Exclusions:** Emergency revascularization for acute limb ischemia; Patients for whom shared decision-making is not feasible (e.g., altered mental status) — clinician-documented
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE C-LD
**Rationale:** Patient-centered care requires that treatment decisions align with patient values and preferences. Shared decision-making improves treatment adherence, patient satisfaction, and outcomes. The 2024 ACC/AHA PAD Guideline emphasizes shared decision-making throughout.

customSections.heading: QM-8 — Post-Revascularization Surveillance (Quality Measure)
customSections.text:
Patients who have undergone lower extremity revascularization who have documented post-procedural surveillance (ABI + duplex ultrasound) within 30 days and at 6 months.

**Numerator:** Patients who underwent lower extremity revascularization who have documented ABI measurement AND duplex ultrasound within 30 days of the procedure.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years who underwent lower extremity revascularization (endovascular or surgical) within the measurement period.
**Exclusions:** Patients for whom post-revascularization surveillance is clinically inappropriate (clinician-documented); Patients who decline post-revascularization surveillance
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE B-NR
**Rationale:** Post-revascularization surveillance detects restenosis, occlusion, or graft failure early, enabling timely re-intervention and improving long-term patency. ABI + duplex ultrasound is the standard surveillance protocol per the 2024 ACC/AHA PAD Guideline.

customSections.heading: Guideline References
customSections.text:
1. Goodney PP, Ross EG, Bruckel JT, et al. 2026 ACC/AHA Clinical Performance and Quality Measures for Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2026 Jan 8. DOI: 10.1016/j.jacc.2025.09.003. PMID: 41505788
2. Gornik HL, Aronow HD, Goodney PP, et al. 2024 ACC/AHA/AACVPR/APMA/ABC/SCAI/SVM/SVN/SVS/SIR/VESS Guideline for the Management of Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease. Circulation. 2024;149(24):e1313–e410. PMID: 38743805

## CPT Procedure / Diagnostic Codes

- **37231** — Revascularization, endovascular, tibial/peroneal artery, unilateral, initial vessel; with transluminal stent placement(s) and atherectomy (includes angioplasty when performed)

**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 3 (Harm) / LOE A
**Rationale:** Tobacco use is the most powerful modifiable risk factor for PAD incidence, progression, and limb loss. Continued smoking after revascularization dramatically worsens outcomes. Cessation counseling + pharmacotherapy is Class 3 (Harm) for continued smoking — meaning continued tobacco use is harmful. PM-6 does NOT have the general clinician-appropriateness exclusion.

### PM-7 — Supervised Exercise Therapy (SET) Referral
Patients with claudication symptoms who are referred to or enrolled in a supervised exercise therapy (SET) program.

**Numerator:** Patients with claudication who have a documented referral to or enrollment in a supervised exercise therapy program.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with PAD and claudication symptoms.
**Exclusions:** Patients who decline supervised exercise therapy referral; Patients with CLTI (rest pain, tissue loss) — SET is not indicated for CLTI
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE A
**Rationale:** Supervised exercise therapy is the most effective non-invasive treatment for claudication, improving walking distance, quality of life, and cardiovascular outcomes. It is a Class 1, LOE A recommendation and is Medicare-covered for symptomatic PAD. PM-7 does NOT have the general clinician-appropriateness exclusion.

## Quality Measures (QM-1 – QM-8)
### QM-1 — Diabetes Management in PAD
Patients with PAD and diabetes mellitus who have HbA1c measured and a documented diabetes management plan.

**Numerator:** Patients with PAD and diabetes who have documented HbA1c measurement AND a diabetes management plan (pharmacotherapy or referral to endocrinology/diabetes educator) at the qualifying encounter.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with established PAD and a diagnosis of diabetes mellitus.
**Exclusions:** Patients for whom diabetes management is clinically inappropriate (clinician-documented); Patients who decline diabetes management
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE B-NR  ·  New in 2026
**Rationale:** Diabetes is a major risk factor for PAD severity, wound healing failure, and amputation. HbA1c target <7% (or individualized) reduces microvascular and macrovascular complications. This is a new 2026 measure reflecting the growing importance of cardiometabolic risk management in PAD.

### QM-2 — Preventive Foot Care
Patients with PAD and diabetes or CLTI who receive preventive foot care education and examination.

**Numerator:** Patients with PAD and diabetes or CLTI who have documented foot examination AND foot care education (self-inspection, footwear, wound prevention) at the qualifying encounter.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with established PAD and either diabetes mellitus or CLTI (rest pain, ischemic ulcer, or gangrene).
**Exclusions:** Patients for whom foot care is clinically inappropriate (clinician-documented); Patients who decline foot care education or examination
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE B-NR  ·  New in 2026
**Rationale:** Foot complications (ulceration, infection, gangrene) are the leading cause of amputation in patients with PAD and diabetes. Preventive foot care reduces amputation rates. This is a new 2026 quality measure.

### QM-3 — Novel Lipid-Lowering Therapy Consideration
Patients with PAD and LDL-C above goal despite maximally tolerated statin therapy who are considered for novel lipid-lowering agents (PCSK9 inhibitors, inclisiran, bempedoic acid, ezetimibe).

**Numerator:** Patients with PAD, LDL-C ≥70 mg/dL despite maximally tolerated statin therapy, who have documented consideration of or prescription for novel lipid-lowering agents.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with established PAD and LDL-C ≥70 mg/dL despite maximally tolerated statin therapy.
**Exclusions:** Patients for whom novel lipid-lowering therapy is clinically inappropriate (clinician-documented); Patients who decline novel lipid-lowering therapy
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 2a (Moderate) / LOE B-R  ·  New in 2026
**Rationale:** PCSK9 inhibitors (evolocumab, alirocumab) reduce MACE in high-risk PAD patients. Bempedoic acid and inclisiran are additional options for statin-intolerant patients. LDL-C <70 mg/dL is the target for very high-risk PAD. This is a new 2026 quality measure reflecting emerging evidence.

### QM-4 — Health Disparities Assessment
Patients with PAD who have race/ethnicity, social determinants of health (SDOH), and access-to-care barriers documented to evaluate disparities in PAD detection and management.

**Numerator:** Patients with PAD who have documented race/ethnicity AND at least one SDOH domain (e.g., food insecurity, housing instability, transportation barriers, insurance status) at the qualifying encounter.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with established PAD.
**Exclusions:** Patients who decline to provide race/ethnicity or SDOH information
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE C-LD  ·  New in 2026
**Rationale:** Black, Hispanic, and low-income patients have significantly higher rates of PAD, amputation, and mortality. Systematic documentation of disparities enables targeted quality improvement. This is a new 2026 quality measure reflecting the ACC/AHA's commitment to health equity.

### QM-5 — Saphenous Vein Assessment Prior to Revascularization
Patients undergoing lower extremity surgical revascularization who have preoperative saphenous vein mapping documented.

**Numerator:** Patients undergoing lower extremity bypass surgery who have documented preoperative duplex ultrasound saphenous vein mapping.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with PAD undergoing lower extremity bypass surgery (femoral-popliteal or femoral-tibial bypass).
**Exclusions:** Patients undergoing endovascular-only revascularization (no bypass surgery planned); Emergency revascularization for acute limb ischemia where preoperative mapping is not feasible; Patients for whom vein mapping is clinically inappropriate (clinician-documented); Patients who decline vein mapping
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE B-NR  ·  New in 2026
**Rationale:** Autologous saphenous vein is the preferred conduit for infrainguinal bypass. Preoperative vein mapping identifies suitable conduit, reduces operative time, and improves patency rates. This is a new 2026 quality measure.

### QM-6 — Multidisciplinary Team Discussion for CLTI
Patients with CLTI who have a documented multidisciplinary team discussion of treatment options (revascularization vs. primary amputation vs. medical management) prior to definitive treatment.

**Numerator:** Patients with CLTI who have documented multidisciplinary team discussion (involving at minimum vascular surgery or IR and wound care or podiatry) prior to definitive treatment.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with CLTI (rest pain, ischemic ulcer, or gangrene) being considered for revascularization or amputation.
**Exclusions:** Patients with acute limb ischemia requiring emergency revascularization; Patients for whom multidisciplinary discussion is not feasible (e.g., rural setting without specialist access) — clinician-documented; Patients who decline multidisciplinary evaluation
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE B-NR  ·  New in 2026
**Rationale:** CLTI is associated with 30% 1-year mortality and 25% major amputation rate. Multidisciplinary team discussions improve limb salvage rates and reduce unnecessary amputations. The BEST-CLI trial demonstrated that surgical bypass with adequate conduit is superior to endovascular therapy in good surgical candidates. This is a new 2026 quality measure.

### QM-7 — Shared Decision-Making Documentation
Patients with PAD who have documented shared decision-making discussion of treatment risks, benefits, and patient preferences.

**Numerator:** Patients with PAD who have documented shared decision-making discussion (including patient preferences, treatment options, risks/benefits) at the qualifying encounter.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years with established PAD being considered for revascularization or major medical therapy change.
**Exclusions:** Emergency revascularization for acute limb ischemia; Patients for whom shared decision-making is not feasible (e.g., altered mental status) — clinician-documented
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE C-LD
**Rationale:** Patient-centered care requires that treatment decisions align with patient values and preferences. Shared decision-making improves treatment adherence, patient satisfaction, and outcomes. The 2024 ACC/AHA PAD Guideline emphasizes shared decision-making throughout.

### QM-8 — Post-Revascularization Surveillance
Patients who have undergone lower extremity revascularization who have documented post-procedural surveillance (ABI + duplex ultrasound) within 30 days and at 6 months.

**Numerator:** Patients who underwent lower extremity revascularization who have documented ABI measurement AND duplex ultrasound within 30 days of the procedure.
**Denominator:** All patients aged ≥18 years who underwent lower extremity revascularization (endovascular or surgical) within the measurement period.
**Exclusions:** Patients for whom post-revascularization surveillance is clinically inappropriate (clinician-documented); Patients who decline post-revascularization surveillance
**Guideline class / LOE:** COR Class 1 (Strong) / LOE B-NR
**Rationale:** Post-revascularization surveillance detects restenosis, occlusion, or graft failure early, enabling timely re-intervention and improving long-term patency. ABI + duplex ultrasound is the standard surveillance protocol per the 2024 ACC/AHA PAD Guideline.
